name: Tax Identification Number (TIN)
issuer: the General Authority for Zakat and Tax (GAZT)
note: Saudi Arabia's sheet (its government's own sheet on the OECD's automatic-exchange portal ('Information on Tax Identification Numbers'; the OECD's index page sits behind a bot check and wasn't opened, the sheet itself came straight back)), read 2026-10-30: (last updated 2 May 2018) the General Authority for Zakat and Tax (GAZT, since renamed the Zakat, Tax and Customs Authority, not stated here) issues a TIN once to each taxpayer; individuals don't get one automatically, only those subject to tax or Zakat on commercial activity, VAT or excise; ten digits: a GCC member-state digit, an eight-digit serial and a check digit (rule not given, `check` left out). The national ID number isn't on this sheet. Read as given on application, to anyone liable. No age, fee or time is stated.

sources.title: OECD AEOI portal, Saudi Arabia: Information on Tax Identification Numbers (the jurisdiction's own sheet)
sources.said: TIN is issued by the General Authority for Zakat and Tax (GAZT) to all taxpayers and withholding entities ... Individual: no If no, instances where individuals are not being automatically issued a TIN are: 1) If the individual is subject to tax or Zakat on commercial activities. ... The (first digit) is the GCC Member State. The (next eight digits) is a serial number. The next digit is a check digit.
